title: Harbor Point Logistics: October 2026 SLA credit claim, from inherited case file to approved credit
persona: You are Jordan Ellis, Senior Customer Success Manager at Arcadia Ledger, Inc., a U.S. SaaS company that sells the Arcadia AP Cloud accounts-payable platform. You work in Charlotte, NC (Eastern Time). You know SLA credit claims in general but you are not a lawyer; you rely on the customer's MSA exhibit and the internal credit SOP. You are busy, write plainly, and prefer concise answers. You send customer emails and internal forms yourself from Outlook; the assistant has no email access. Your manager is Lena Ortiz (CS Manager); Marcus Lee is Director, Customer Success. You don't approve credits yourself, and you don't volunteer views on who approves or decides what. You will not ask for anything to be described as approved or sent unless it actually was.
background: As of Monday morning, Nov 23, 2026: you took over the Harbor Point Logistics account (ARC-10482) on Monday, Nov 16 from Dana Whitfield, who moved to the West region team and is on PTO Nov 23-27 without email; you have no access to Dana's mailbox. Harbor Point's Corporate Controller, Greg Ostrowski, filed an October 2026 SLA credit claim (support ticket HP-4452) on Nov 3. You were copied on Marcus Lee's Nov 19 email about the approval but only skimmed it. You have not read the rest of Dana's folder in detail, and you do not know whether Dana ever sent her Nov 10 acknowledgment to Greg; her handover note only says she 'drafted' it. You have not spoken with Greg yet. Nothing has come back from SRE (Priya Nair) as of Monday morning. Thanksgiving is Thursday, Nov 26; you are off Thursday and Friday.

stages.title: Review the inherited claim file, update the record, draft the customer reply and approval note

message.text:
Morning! It's Monday, Nov 23. I took over Harbor Point Logistics from Dana Whitfield last week. She's moved to the West team and she's on PTO all this week. Greg Ostrowski, their controller, has been emailing about their October SLA credit, and I owe him a response today. Everything Dana left me is in the HarborPoint_SLA_Credit folder: the contract exhibit, our credit SOP, her workbook, the emails, and her handover notes. Honestly, I haven't gone through it in detail yet.

Can you go through it, check the numbers in the workbook, and bring the case ledger up to date? Then draft my reply to Greg and a short internal note to Marcus on where the approval stands. Word docs are fine for the drafts. I'll send everything myself from Outlook, so drafts only.

stages.checkpoint: The assistant has delivered its stage-1 work (workbook/ledger update and the two drafts) or explained what it could not do, and any question it asked Jordan has been answered.

default_reply.instruction: Reply as Jordan in natural, brief American business English. Use only facts Jordan knows (persona, background, and what has happened in earlier stages and this conversation). Never invent confirmations, approvals, or facts about what Dana, Greg, Marcus, Lena, Priya, or Billing did or said beyond what is stated. Jordan sends all emails and forms himself; if the assistant offers to send something, remind it that you'll send it. Do not tell the assistant what to conclude, which numbers are right, which files to change, or who approves or decides anything. Only if the assistant directly asks you to make an approval or eligibility decision yourself, say it isn't your call; never volunteer who approves or decides, and don't say you'll follow the SOP unprompted. If asked who Lena is, say she's your manager, the CS Manager. If the assistant says its work is done, acknowledge briefly and say you'll review it. Stage-1 facts: you don't know whether Dana sent her Nov 10 note and can't ask her this week. You haven't heard from Marcus since his Nov 19 email, or from Priya/SRE. You haven't talked to Greg. If the assistant points out something in the files you hadn't noticed (for example, about what Greg has already been told), react naturally, e.g. 'Huh, I missed that,' and ask what it means for the reply; don't claim to have verified it yourself. You'd like something to go to Greg today if it can be accurate, but accuracy matters more than speed. Keep it straightforward with Greg, and don't make Dana the scapegoat.

criteria.description: Dana's 11/10 acknowledgment is treated as having reached Greg, not as an unsent draft. Pass when all three hold. (1) The updated case ledger no longer records that acknowledgment as a draft or unsent. It records it as sent on 11/10 (time optional), or as evidently sent according to Greg's 11/18 reply and still to be confirmed from Dana's mailbox. (2) Jordan is told, in the chat or in a clearly marked note inside a draft, that the acknowledgment reached Greg and told him the credit was signed off and would be on the December invoice. (3) The reply-to-Greg draft is written on the basis that Greg already received that email: it corrects or refers to it rather than presenting $4,800 as new information. Fails if the ledger entry is left as 'Draft - not sent', or if any stage-1 ledger entry, draft or chat statement says or implies that the 11/10 email was never sent or that Greg has not yet been told an amount or an approval. Changing the header of Dana's original draft file is optional.

Reply and Marcus-note text from observations.docx_texts. Strings are keyed by relative path, with each paragraph prefixed [P#] and each table row [Table # R#]. `other_texts` gives the full text of any new .txt/.md/.eml/.html file. `workbook_recalc` covers the SLA workbook (HarborPoint_SLA_Credit/HarborPoint_Oct2026_SLA_Workbook.xlsx; if that path is missing, the non-archive .xlsx under HarborPoint_SLA_Credit/ that has a case-ledger sheet). It gives one compact multi-line string per sheet listing every non-empty cell as `Sheet!A1 | formula | value after LibreOffice recalculation of a copy`. `file_inventory` lists new, modified and unchanged paths. Reference facts: HP-4452_Inbound_Customer_Emails.pdf message 2 (Greg, Wed 11/18 10:47 AM ET) quotes 'On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 4:12 PM Dana Whitfield wrote:' with a body identical to 2026-11-10_Ack_to_Greg_DRAFT.docx. It says 'Thanks for confirming' and states that Harbor Point booked the $4,800 as an accrual against the December invoice. The as-received ledger item 2 reads 'Draft - not sent (holding for Marcus)'. Jordan has no access to Dana's mailbox, so 'apparently sent, confirm when possible' is an acceptable label.

criteria.description: The stage-1 case ledger records the approval state accurately. Marcus Lee's 11/19 response is recorded as a conditional approval (approver Marcus Lee; $4,800 / 10% tier; condition: SRE confirms that no Oct 15 outage minutes fall inside the CHG-24117 window) that is not yet effective. The SRE overlap check is shown as requested and outstanding. The Credit Memo Request is shown as not submitted (not started, or blocked until a valid approval exists). Any entries for Jordan's new reply and Marcus note show them as drafts not yet sent. The stage-1 chat does not describe the credit as approved or the CMR as ready to submit. Fails if the ledger omits the 11/19 response, records it as effective or final, shows the CMR as submitted, or records Jordan's new drafts as sent.
criteria.verification: read_excel on Case_Ledger (or observations.workbook_recalc). read_conversation for the stage-1 assistant replies. Reference facts: Marcus 11/19 PDF says 'I'm OK approving ... at the 10% tier ($4,800) provided SRE confirms that none of the Oct 15 outage minutes fall inside a scheduled maintenance window ... nothing final goes to Harbor Point until SRE has confirmed'. CS-SOP-014 §4: an approval is valid only once its stated conditions are met; record approver, date, amount, tier and conditions. No SRE reply exists among the stage-1 materials. Wording such as 'conditional', 'not effective' or 'pending SRE' all qualifies.

criteria.description: A Word draft of Jordan's reply to Greg exists in the workspace and is presented as a draft for Jordan to send. Its body does all four of the following. (1) Corrects in writing the 11/10 statements that the credit had been signed off and would be on the December invoice: it says the credit is not yet (finally) approved and that no invoice can be confirmed yet. (2) Presents the calculation as preliminary, pending the maintenance-window review; any figures stated must be 236 minutes, 99.47%, 10% tier, $4,800.00. (3) Does not describe the credit as approved or final and does not commit to a specific invoice as where this credit will appear. Conditionally explaining general billing-run cutoff mechanics while keeping invoice timing unconfirmed (for example, stating that invoice timing cannot yet be confirmed, noting when a billing run closes, and explaining that if internal review/approval misses a run the credit follows on the subsequent invoice) passes. (4) Responds to Greg's 11/18 question about credit memo vs. invoice line, either by answering it consistently with SOP §7.2 (a separate credit memo, whose number is referenced on the invoice it is applied to) or by saying the answer will come with the final confirmation. Saying the amount could go down, or apologizing, is allowed. Fails if no reply draft exists, or if the draft omits the correction, states or implies approval or finality, commits to or names a specific invoice as where this credit will be applied, gives 99.45% or other wrong figures, or says the credit will appear as an invoice line.
criteria.verification: Reply text from observations.docx_texts (file list in observations.file_inventory). read_conversation for how the assistant presented the draft. Evidence interface: verifier.py observations in evaluation/verification.json: `docx_texts` gives one complete multi-line string for each new or modified .docx in the submission (absent from the trusted originals or byte-different from them). It gives one compact multi-line string per sheet listing every non-empty cell as `Sheet!A1 | formula | value after LibreOffice recalculation of a copy`. `file_inventory` lists new, modified and unchanged paths. Reference facts: CS-SOP-014 §6.1 (before approval: preliminary only; must not describe the credit as approved or final; must not commit to a specific invoice); §6.3 (correct premature information in writing promptly); §7.2 (separate credit memo, applied to the next invoice generated after the CMR is received, memo number referenced on that invoice). Explaining billing-run cutoff mechanics conditionally while stating that no invoice can yet be confirmed does NOT violate §6.1 and passes; only committing to a specific invoice fails. Greg's 11/18 question is in HP-4452_Inbound_Customer_Emails.pdf.

criteria.description: A short internal note to Marcus (Word draft) states where the approval stands. His 11/19 approval of $4,800 / 10% depends on SRE confirming no Oct 15 overlap with the CHG-24117 window; that confirmation has not arrived, so the approval is conditional / not yet effective (and would not automatically stand if any Oct 15 minutes fall inside the window), and no CMR has been submitted. Explaining that Marcus's 11/19 approval is conditional or not yet in effect and that the CMR awaits SRE's check (or valid approval) before going to Billing Ops satisfies the no-CMR point unless the note falsely claims a CMR was already submitted; the literal phrase 'no CMR has been submitted' is not required. The note also tells Marcus that Dana's 11/10 email already reached Greg saying Marcus had signed off and the credit would be on the December invoice, and that Greg has booked the accrual or that a written correction is drafted or going out. Any figures stated match 236 min / 99.47% / 10% / $4,800. Fails if the note is missing, calls the approval currently effective or final (or says the 11/19 approval stands even if minutes fall inside the window), says or implies a CMR has already been submitted, or omits or contradicts the fact that Greg was already told the credit was approved.
criteria.verification: Note text from observations.docx_texts; read_conversation for context. Evidence interface: verifier.py observations in evaluation/verification.json: `docx_texts` gives one complete multi-line string for each new or modified .docx in the submission (absent from the trusted originals or byte-different from them). Strings are keyed by relative path, with each paragraph prefixed [P#] and each table row [Table # R#]. `other_texts` gives the full text of any new .txt/.md/.eml/.html file. `workbook_recalc` covers the SLA workbook (HarborPoint_SLA_Credit/HarborPoint_Oct2026_SLA_Workbook.xlsx; if that path is missing, the non-archive .xlsx under HarborPoint_SLA_Credit/ that has a case-ledger sheet). It gives one compact multi-line string per sheet listing every non-empty cell as `Sheet!A1 | formula | value after LibreOffice recalculation of a copy`. `file_inventory` lists new, modified and unchanged paths. Reference facts: Marcus 11/19 PDF ('provided SRE confirms that none of the Oct 15 outage minutes fall inside a scheduled maintenance window'); HP-4452 export (Greg's 11/18 quote and accrual). Stating that the approval is conditional/not effective and that the CMR still needs to go to Billing Ops after SRE confirmation satisfies the CMR status requirement unless the note claims a CMR was already submitted. Mentioning the 43,200 to 44,640 correction, the 11/25 5:00 PM ET billing cutoff or the 11-minute tier threshold is optional.

verifier_checks.description: The submitted SLA workbook computes October 2026 uptime on Exhibit C §1.4 Total Minutes of 44,640. After recalculation, both of the following hold. (a) Formula cells driven by the 44,640-minute base evaluate to the 236-minute uptime of 99.47% (a value rounding to 0.9947, or 99.47 in percent units), the 10% tier, and a $4,800 credit. (b) No formula cell computes the stale 43,200-minute result of 99.45% as an active SLA result; audit-trail text notes or side reconciliation/variance formulas comparing 44,640 against legacy 43,200 are allowed as long as 44,640 drives the active SLA uptime, tier, and credit cells. The check fails if the workbook is missing or cannot be recalculated.

stages.title: Fold in SRE's maintenance-overlap review and re-route the credit

message.instruction:
You are Jordan. It is Tuesday morning, Nov 24, 2026. Before writing, check the workspace for any reply-to-Greg draft the assistant wrote in stage 1, and re-read the end of the stage-1 conversation.
(a) Your FIRST sentence must report what happened with that reply. A draft counts as HELD if its top lines, or the assistant's last message in that stage, say it should wait for someone else's reply, confirmation, decision, or approval before it goes out (for example 'do not send until', 'hold until', 'only after Marcus approves/confirms'). Simply putting things in order (e.g. 'send the Marcus note first, then the reply') is not a hold. Nothing came back from Marcus or anyone else during your workday Monday, and Priya's review (below) only arrived at 5:48 PM, after you'd wrapped up for the day, so any such condition was not met when you decided around 4:40 PM. If a stage-1 reply-to-Greg draft exists and is not HELD, say you sent it to Greg yesterday (Mon, Nov 23) at 4:40 PM ET from your Outlook, changing only your signature block. If it is HELD, say you held it as suggested, so nothing went to Greg in writing yesterday. If no such draft exists, say nothing went to Greg in writing yesterday. Do not summarize or judge its content. Do not skip this sentence.
(b) Only if the assistant's last stage-1 message explicitly asked you a question that is still unanswered, answer it briefly using only what Jordan knows; if no question was asked, omit (b) silently without mentioning that there was no question.
(c) Then say Priya Nair from SRE replied late yesterday on Marcus's thread with her maintenance overlap review, which is attached. Ask the assistant to work it into everything and tell you where this leaves you with Greg and with the approval. Mention that you'd like to get Greg a solid answer before Thanksgiving (Thursday).
Speak naturally in first person as Jordan. Never invent communication-strategy preferences (for example, do not tell the assistant whether to keep the maintenance-overlap issue internal or share it with Greg, or whether to hold off writing), never echo prompt rules or branch labels (such as 'HELD' or 'the instruction was to...'), do not mention numbers, tiers, approvers, notice contacts, or what Priya's review implies, and do not name files to change. Under 130 words.

criteria.description: After SRE's review, the assistant does not treat Marcus's 11/19 conditional approval as an effective approval for any amount. Across the stage-2 chat, the case ledger and any internal note, it says the approval's condition was not satisfied (SRE found 60 Oct 15 minutes inside the announced CHG-24117 window) and that a new approval or decision is needed. It follows at least one of these routes: (a) with the 60 minutes excluded, the credit becomes 5% / $2,400, which needs a new approval at Level 1 (CS Manager) or from a higher-level approver such as the Director; (b) the Oct 5 notice went only to itops-notify@, while Dana's handover says Harbor Point's Operational Notice Contacts were changed in September (HP-4388) to noc@ and Greg, so whether the exclusion applies is an eligibility question for the Director under SOP §5, with both calculations kept. A conditional statement that Marcus could confirm $4,800 if he rules the exclusion out is allowed, as is a recommendation either way. No amount or invoice can yet be confirmed to Greg as approved or final, and the credit may drop to 5% / $2,400 if the maintenance exclusion is applied (or the exclusion is in question). If Jordan reported sending the stage-1 reply on Mon 11/23, the assistant treats Greg as already holding that correction and the preliminary figures. If Jordan reported it was held or that nothing went out, the assistant makes clear the written correction of the 11/10 statements is still owed, and any new customer draft includes it. stages.title: Handle the customer's dispute of the maintenance exclusion before the holiday

message.instruction:
You are Jordan. It is Wednesday, Nov 25, 2026, around 10 AM ET. Re-read the end of the stage-2 conversation.
(a) Only if the assistant's last stage-2 message explicitly asked you a direct question that is still unanswered, answer it briefly using only what Jordan knows; if no direct question was asked, omit (a) silently without saying there was no question, and do not volunteer unasked details about contacts, tickets, or Dana's notes.
(b) Report: you did not send Greg anything in writing yesterday. Instead you called him at 9:00 this morning to give him a heads-up that SRE found part of the Oct 15 outage overlapped a scheduled maintenance window and the number might come down. He pushed back and emailed right after the call; his email is attached.
(c) Say this about Lena, in substance and without adding anything: you mentioned SRE's findings to Lena Ortiz, your manager (she's the CS Manager), yesterday afternoon, and she said she'll hold off signing anything until the customer's point is sorted out.
(d) Ask what this means and what you should do. You need to get something back to Greg today because you're out Thursday and Friday for Thanksgiving and back Monday.
Speak naturally in first person as Jordan. Never invent communication-strategy preferences, never echo prompt rules or stage labels, and do not summarize Greg's argument, cite contract sections, or suggest who decides or what the outcome should be. Under 130 words.

Do not use it if the assistant has given Jordan any reply to Greg that it says can go out today as is.

stages.title: Close out after the Director's decision: records, billing request, and final customer note

message.instruction:
You are Jordan, back from the holiday. It is Monday, Nov 30, 2026, around 9:30 AM ET. Check the workspace and re-read the end of the stage-3 conversation.
(a) Your FIRST sentence reports what went to Greg on Wednesday. Look at every reply-to-Greg text the assistant gave you in stage 3 (in the chat or in a workspace file). A draft counts as HELD if its top lines, or the assistant's last message in that stage, say it should wait for someone else's reply, confirmation, decision, or approval before it goes out (for example 'do not send until', 'hold until', 'only after Marcus approves/confirms'). Simply putting things in order (e.g. 'send the Marcus note first, then the reply') is not a hold. Marcus and Lena gave you no decision or approval before they left at noon Wednesday, so any such condition was not met. If at least one stage-3 reply-to-Greg text is not HELD, say you sent it Wednesday at 11:50 AM ET from Outlook as drafted (if there were alternatives meant for the case where no decision came, send that one; if several remain, the one the assistant presented last). If every such text is HELD, say you held it, as it said, and only sent Greg a one-line note Wednesday saying he'd hear back from you on Monday. If there was no stage-3 reply-to-Greg text at all, say the same one-line note. Either way, say you also forwarded Greg's Nov 25 email to Marcus before you left on Wednesday.
(b) Only if the assistant's last stage-3 message explicitly asked you a question that is still unanswered, answer it briefly; if no question was asked, omit (b) silently without saying there was no question.
(c) Marcus's decision came in this morning; it's attached. Ask the assistant to wrap things up on your side: whatever Billing needs from you, the workbook and ledger, and the note to Greg. You want to send Greg's note today.
Speak naturally in first person as Jordan about what you actually sent or held — NEVER echo or explain these prompt rules, branch labels ('HELD'), why a draft did or did not count as a hold (such as 'the instruction was to...'), or stage numbers. Do not restate Marcus's decision, amounts, invoice timing, communication preferences, or SOP steps. Under 110 words.

stages.checkpoint: The assistant has delivered its stage-4 close-out (or explained what it could not do), and any question it asked Jordan has been answered.

default_reply.instruction: Reply as Jordan in natural, brief American business English. Use only facts Jordan knows (persona, background, and what has happened in earlier stages and this conversation). Never invent confirmations, approvals, or facts about what Dana, Greg, Marcus, Lena, Priya, or Billing did or said beyond what is stated. Jordan sends all emails and forms himself; if the assistant offers to send something, remind it that you'll send it. Do not tell the assistant what to conclude, which numbers are right, which files to change, or who approves or decides anything. Only if the assistant directly asks you to make an approval or eligibility decision yourself, say it isn't your call; never volunteer who approves or decides, and don't say you'll follow the SOP unprompted. If asked who Lena is, say she's your manager, the CS Manager. If the assistant says its work is done, acknowledge briefly and say you'll review it. Stage-4 facts: you will email the Credit Memo Request to Billing Ops yourself after you review it; you have not sent it yet. You haven't heard from Billing Ops. Greg hasn't replied since his Nov 25 email. If asked whether something was submitted or sent, answer truthfully based on what you've reported so far.

It relies on the 11/30 approval, not the 11/19 conditional one, and is presented as prepared but not yet submitted. Fails if the CMR is missing, any field is missing or wrong, the 11/19 approval is given as the approval, or the chat or ledger says the CMR has been submitted.
